report.summary: Cause: `load()` in `public/src/store.js` let every response write to the screen state, so a slow earlier response could arrive after a later one. Opening Orders starts a load for the current filter (All). Clicking Shipped quickly starts a second one. If the All response arrived last, it replaced the Shipped list with new and packed orders. This breaks ORD-2. Fix: each `load()` now takes a sequence number, and only the most recently started load may update the state, on success or failure. Responses from older loads are ignored, so a stale failure can't show an error either. I added a regression test in `test/store.test.js` that resolves the older request after the newer one.
report.verification: `npm test` passes (5/5). With the store fix reverted, the new test fails (4 pass, 1 fail). With the fix restored, all 5 pass. I did not drive the browser UI or run the Recovery Probe checks. Those checks cover failed reads, not out-of-order responses, so they don't address this race.
